subject: botany

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack botany section, Chapter 4 Plant Kingdom, book p.8, SAQ 2. The book's first table row is grammatically garbled by the scan ('Plant body is gametophyte exhibit Young Protonema and adult gametophore'); the facts are standard and are written cleanly here. Only one source book is held for botany — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card, not merely unrun. The four-row 1-mark-each split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

steps.label: Plant body
lines: Mosses: gametophyte in two stages — a
creeping protonema and a leafy, erect
steps.why: The first difference is visible to the eye: a flat green thallus in liverworts against the two-stage moss gametophyte that ends as a leafy shoot.
common_mistakes: Calling the leafy moss plant a sporophyte — the leafy body is still the gametophyte.
Writing that liverworts have stems and leaves — the thallus has neither.
steps.memory_tip: Liverwort = a flat liver-shaped lobe; moss = a tiny leafy shoot — picture the two shapes side by side.
steps.margin_note: One contrast row = one mark; keep both sides in every row.

steps.label: Vegetative reproduction
lines: thallus and by gemmae in gemma cups.
Mosses: by fragmentation and budding in
steps.why: Both groups fragment; the special organ differs — gemmae in gemma cups belong to liverworts, budding in the secondary protonema belongs to mosses.
common_mistakes: Giving gemma cups to mosses — gemma cups belong to liverworts (Marchantia).
steps.memory_tip: One special organ each: liverwort → gemma cup; moss → secondary protonema.
steps.margin_note: Name the special organ on each side; fragmentation alone is not a difference.

steps.label: Position of sex organs
lines: develop on the same or different thalli.
Mosses: sex organs develop at the apex of
steps.why: Both groups make the same organs; this row asks only WHERE they sit — on the thallus in liverworts, at the shoot apex in mosses.
common_mistakes: Describing the organs' structure instead of their position — this row is about where they develop.
steps.memory_tip: Apex is the moss word for this row — moss organs sit at the top of the leafy shoot.
steps.margin_note: One line per side; the word 'apex' carries the moss half.

steps.label: Spore dispersal
lines: Liverwort capsules have elaters that help
Moss capsules open by peristome teeth —
steps.why: The capsule differs in its dispersal machinery: elaters in liverworts, a ring of peristome teeth in mosses — the book's fourth row and the standard one.
common_mistakes: Swapping elaters and peristome teeth between the two groups.
steps.memory_tip: Pair by letters: Liverwort–Elaters, Moss–Peristome (L–E, M–P).
steps.margin_note: Any four correct rows earn full marks; these four are the book's own.

insider_note: Keep each row about ONE feature on both sides — a mixed list of unrelated points on each side is the common way this table loses marks.
